stops.note: a paid teacher of wisdom and rhetoric, whom Plato portrayed as a clever arguer for hire
'adulterated, falsified', from sophisticare 'to use sophistry, to tamper with'
first meant 'not pure', of adulterated wine or drugs; 'worldly-wise' came in the late 1800s and 'technically advanced' in the 1940s

current_meaning: having worldly experience and refined taste; highly developed and complex
